findings.reason: the 12 KB bound and the moved set are both derived from this pair, so a reader cannot tell which measurement supports the decision.
findings.text: the paragraph reports "with the six fields and seven further dispatch-time fields gone, 16 of 57 pointers stayed at or above 8 KB; with every field below moved as well, 25 of 57 stayed at or above 8 KB" — moving more fields off a pointer can only shrink it, so a superset move cannot raise the count at or above a fixed threshold; one of the two figures is mislabelled (or its population differs from the other's) and neither can be the basis for the bound

findings.reason: the third node's done-when requires "none at or above 12 KB", a measure over a field set the population has already outgrown, so the node would fail on data it cannot change by doing the work.
findings.text: the paragraph concludes "The lead decided on 2026-11-05 that the bound is 12 KB, just above the largest pointer that set leaves" from a 2026-11-02 sample of 57 pointers, but the same simulation over today's live crew home (114 pointers, 2026-11-05) leaves a largest pointer of 17,984 bytes and 8 pointers at or above 12 KB after every one of the fifteen declared fields is removed; the largest remainder is `r-20261102T204241022825-coil-edit-fine-panels` (orientation_check 3,422 B, node 3,404 B, detail 1,492 B), fields the plan does not move

findings.reason: without a stated rule for those two fields the node must invent the measurement, and the number it records cannot be reconciled with the bound the plan asserts.
findings.text: "a frozen copy of the live crew home's pointers, taken when the third node starts … re-read with the moved fields served from their detail files" is not executable for the two fields that node exists to move: at its start no live pointer has a detail file for `dispatch_options` or `suite_evidence` (the third node is what writes them at launch), so the two fields carrying 31–158 KB per pointer cannot be served from a detail file and the measure does not say what value they take

findings.reason: a node told there is no reader will move the field and break those three tests, failing the section's own "tests that read each moved field pass" measure and costing a repair node.
findings.text: `suite_evidence` "moves with no reader to route" is false outside `reckon/`: three tests read it off the live pointer — `runs.read_pointer(RUN)["suite_evidence"]` at `tests/test_the_landing_pass_measures_and_lands.py:309`, `:341` and `:782` — and the section's `ast` walk is scoped to `reckon/` alone, which is why the gap is invisible to it
